newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan CPC awards second Jan-Jun diesel contract.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC awards second Jan-Jun diesel contract.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has awarded its second diesel sale contract for cargoes to be lifted from January to June 1997, a CPC official said on Tuesday.
The second contract was awarded at a premium of 45-50 cents per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, on a free-on-board (fob) basis from Kaohsiung, he said.
The award was made at the same premium as the first contract, he said.
Market sources said the awarded price was at a 46-cent premium to Singapore spot quotes, fob.
The CPC official said both contracts were awarded to the same oil trading firm.
Market sources said the contracts were won by Singapore trader Hin Leong Trading.
Under each contract, CPC would export four to six 225,000-to-250,000-barrel cargoes of 0.3-percent sulphur diesel.
The term tender attracted more than 10 bidders, the official said.
